For this purpose, thirty-one 2nd grade elementary students at a primary school in Ahvaz city were selected as the subjects of the study. The participants were assigned into an experimental group of 18 subjects and a control group of 13 subjects based on the convenience sampling. The data was collected by using a pretest and post-test with 20 vocabulary items selected from a textbook for 2nd grade elementary students. In the experimental group, we used self-regulation in the experimental conditions and the control group used the traditional teaching method in their classrooms. Data was analyzed by using descriptive statistics, independent samples t-test, and multivariate analysis of variance. The results of the research showed that there is a significant difference between the post-test scores of the experimental and control groups. Furthermore, the results revealed a significant effect of using self-regulation on improving the vocabulary knowledge of 2nd grade elementary students. Hello! I’m SO excited to share this nail art with you today. For the first time ever, I am joining up with a group of gorgeous ladies to bring you a nail art challenge. Each month we’re challenging ourselves to create nails inspired by a theme or color palette.

I recently took the trip to Ottawa to attend a symposium on Social Media for the Criminal Justice system, held by the Ottawa Police. One of the speakers, Ryan Hemsworth was a bit of a surprise. Ryan is a local celebrity here in Ottawa, known for his work at the Ottawa Citizen, the Ottawa Journal and, most notably, the Ottawa Red Blacks, and their cheerleading squad, The Ottawa Red Blackettes. It is no secret that Ottawa is the city of cheerleaders, and Ryan himself is a member of the cheerleading squad. When he was invited to speak, Ryan was more than willing to accept, but he wanted to talk about something other than himself, and something other than cheerleading.
Ryan, with his lovely smile and infectious laugh, spoke about the importance of Social Media and how he as a member of the Red Blackettes can use it to its full potential, and still maintain a professional image. The way that Ryan spoke of social media, of Facebook, Twitter and all of the other social media outlets that are available, was quite impressive. He had a wonderful sense of humour that came through in his speech, and it was very entertaining to listen to.
The other speakers at the event spoke of the more serious side of social media. They spoke of the importance of not only learning how to use social media as a tool to increase the efficiency of the criminal justice system, but they also spoke of the dangers of using social media to further criminal activity. The speakers, which included the head of the Canadian Criminal Justice Association, also emphasized the importance of social media for crime prevention. They spoke of how using social media can allow for faster communication, which will help to prevent and stop crimes before they happen.
Ryan’s presentation was the highlight of the symposium, and it was nice to see a local celebrity use his social media status to give a lecture, instead of just being another celebrity.
While attending the symposium, I asked Ryan if he thought that he would continue to use social media to promote himself, and he said that he absolutely would, as he wants to be able to use it to keep in touch with his friends, and fans.
I have no doubt that Ryan will go on to use social media in the future, and I am sure that he will continue to be as entertaining as he was at the symposium, and his fans and friends will love to hear his stories.
